crisisResources.heading: Support is available
crisisResources.intro: If things feel like a lot right now, you can reach people who are there to help — any time, and separately from this report.
crisisResources.disclaimer: These are independent services, not part of Rectifia. Rectifia is not an emergency service and cannot contact any of them for you or send help on your behalf. Rectifia cannot see that you have opened this panel, and does not record it. If someone is in immediate danger, please use the emergency number for where you are.

authLayout.description: Rectifia is the workplace reporting and case-management platform behind confidential disclosures, investigations, and compliance deadlines.

confidential.title: Confidential by design
confidential.body: Reports are handled on a need-to-know basis, and each role only ever sees the case data it is entitled to.

deadlines.title: Deadlines tracked for you
deadlines.body: Acknowledgment and feedback windows are calculated per jurisdiction and counted down on every case.

routing.title: Routed to the right handler
routing.body: Category and department rules assign new cases automatically the moment they are submitted.

publicEntry.title: Rectifia
publicEntry.description: Confidential workplace reporting. Choose where you're headed.

trackCard.body: Already filed a report? Enter the Case ID and passcode you were given at the time to read your handler's replies and send a message back. No account, no sign-in.

alert.title: Filing a new report starts with your employer's link
alert.body: Reports go to one specific company, so they can only be filed through the reporting link or QR code your employer published - on a noticeboard, an intranet page, or a handbook. There is no way to look a company up from here. If you don't have the link, ask however your workplace shares it.

staffCard.title: Staff sign in
staffCard.body: For case handlers, HR coordinators, managers, and administrators with a Rectifia account.

publicEntry.lostCredentials: Lost your Case ID or passcode? Neither is stored in a form anyone can read back, so they cannot be recovered or reset - not by us, and not by your employer. Filing a new report is the only way forward.

invalidLink.title: This reporting link isn't valid
invalidLink.description: We couldn't find the company for this link.
invalidLink.alertBody: The link you followed doesn't point to a company that accepts reports through Rectifia. Double-check the address, or ask whoever shared it for a current one.
invalidLink.tempUnavailable: If this keeps happening, the reporting service may be temporarily unavailable.

anonymous.label: Stay anonymous
anonymous.detail: No name, email, or phone number is recorded anywhere on this report - not encrypted, not stored blank, simply never collected. Nobody at your employer, nobody at Rectifia, and nobody with a court order can look you up afterwards. You can still read replies and answer questions using your Case ID and passcode. Be aware that some investigations are harder to complete this way, and a few cannot be resolved at all, because the investigator has no way to come back to you for the detail they need.

confidential.label: Be identifiable to the investigator only
confidential.summary: Only the person assigned to your case sees who you are.
confidential.detail: Choosing this records your choice - it does not collect anything yet. You are not asked for your details on this screen. When you open your case, you'll be able to give the investigator your name, email, phone, or whatever you're willing to share; it is encrypted the moment you submit it, and never appears on any dashboard, in any report, or to anyone else at your employer. The investigator can come back to you with follow-up questions once you do, which usually makes a case easier to resolve. Nothing requires you to do this by a deadline, and leaving it blank is a choice you can make too.

harassment.description: Unwanted conduct targeting you or someone else - verbal, written, physical, or visual.

toxicManagement.label: Toxic management
toxicManagement.description: A pattern of behavior from a manager that's undermining your wellbeing or ability to work.

retaliation.label: Retaliation
retaliation.description: Being treated worse after raising a concern, or after supporting someone who did.

burnout.label: Burnout

dataHandlingNotice.title: Before you continue

points.aiProcessing: Your answers are processed by an AI system (Anthropic) that structures your report, scores its urgency and detail completeness, and suggests where it should be routed — it never determines whether policy was broken and never decides your case's outcome; that is always a person's call.
points.tierChoice: Choosing to stay anonymous later means no name, email, or phone number is ever collected; choosing to be confidential means only your assigned investigator can ever learn who you are, and only if you choose to tell them.
points.credentials: You'll get a Case ID and a one-time passcode when you file — if you lose either, they cannot be recovered or reset.

errors.incomplete: Please answer every question before submitting.

evidence.title: Attach evidence
evidence.body: A screenshot, a document, or a photo can identify you even when your written answers don't - a filename, the content itself, or details hidden in a photo's file information can all carry your name. Attaching anything here is entirely your choice; you can also skip this and add files later from your case thread once you have your Case ID and passcode.
evidence.fileTypeNote: PDF, images, plain text, CSV, or Office documents, up to 25MB each.

pulseSurveyForm.description: A few quick questions about how work is going at {{company}}. Takes under a minute.

previewAlert.title: Preview - nothing is recorded
previewAlert.body: This is exactly what employees see. You can click through the scale and type in the boxes; nothing you enter here is saved, sent, or counted anywhere.

liveVersion.title: This is the live version, not your draft
liveVersion.body: You have unpublished changes. This preview shows what employees are receiving right now. Publish to make your changes part of what is sent.

caseAccess.hint: Both were shown to you once, when you submitted your report.

errors.invalid: Case ID or passcode is incorrect.

saved.title: An email address is saved for updates
saved.body: When there is an update on your case we send a short, deliberately vague message to that address — it never mentions your case, this company, or what you reported. You still open your case here with your Case ID and passcode.
saved.removeNote: Removing it deletes the address completely. Notifications stop; nothing else about your case changes.

offer.title: Want to be emailed when there is an update?
offer.body: Optional. Without it, you check back here whenever you like — nothing is lost by leaving this alone.

form.title: Adding an email address for updates

whatThisCreates.title: What this creates
whatThisCreates.body: Saving an address creates a stored link between that address and this case. That link is exactly what “anonymous” otherwise guarantees does not exist. It is encrypted and nobody working on your case can read it — not your handler, not the HR Coordinator, not your Company Admin — but it exists, and you should decide knowing that rather than find out later.

throwaway.title: A throwaway address is a fine choice
throwaway.body: A free burner address you make for this and nothing else works perfectly well here, and for many people it is the sensible option. We would rather say that plainly than have you use a work address because we stayed quiet about it.

whatEmailsSay.title: What the emails say
whatEmailsSay.body: As little as possible, on purpose. Something like “You have an update” and a link to our front page — never your Case ID, the category, the status, or anything about this company. Anyone glancing at your inbox learns nothing.

takeItBack.title: You can take it back
takeItBack.body1: Remove it at any time from this page and the address is deleted, not just switched off.
takeItBack.body2: This does not change who can see your report or affect how your case is handled, and your case stays anonymous either way.

form.emailHint: Keep hold of your Case ID and passcode either way — this address cannot be used to recover them.

whatDoesNotChange.title: What does not change
whatDoesNotChange.subjectNeverSees: The person your report is about never sees your name, or that you gave one.
whatDoesNotChange.hrNeverSees: The HR Coordinator who oversees the case queue never sees it.
whatDoesNotChange.adminNeverSees: Your Company Admin never sees it.
whatDoesNotChange.nothingElseChanges: Nothing you have already written in this case changes, and no message is sent to anyone asking about it.

cannotBeUndone.title: This cannot be undone
cannotBeUndone.body1: Once your details are stored they stay part of this case's record until it ends. We are not offering an undo button, because it could not mean what it says: removing your details from a live investigation would destroy part of its record, and leaving them in place while telling you they were gone would not be true.
cannotBeUndone.body2: You are under no obligation to do this. Your case is worked the same way either way, and if you would rather stay anonymous, close this and carry on.

identityPanel.giveAsMuchAsYouWant: Give as much or as little as you want — one detail is enough. Anything you leave blank is simply not stored.

fields.name: Your name
fields.emailHint: For the investigator to reach you directly. This is separate from update notifications, which never contain case details.
fields.notes: Anything else you want them to know
fields.confirmHint: Typed out in full, so this is never something that happens on a stray click.

upgrade.collapsedBody: Nobody working on this case knows who you are, and nothing here will ask you to change that. If you would rather the investigator could contact you directly, you can choose to tell them who you are.
upgrade.expandedTitle: Telling the investigator who you are
upgrade.whatChanges: The handler assigned to your case will be able to see the details you give below. They are encrypted when stored, the handler has to give a written reason to decrypt them, and every time anyone looks it is recorded.
upgrade.submitLabel: Tell the investigator who I am
upgrade.doneTitle: Your details are on the case
upgrade.doneBody: The handler assigned to your case can now find out who you are. Nobody else can, and nobody was told to ask you for this.

provide.collapsedTitle: You chose to be identifiable to the investigator
provide.collapsedBody: When you filed this report, you chose to let the investigator know who you are. That choice was recorded, but no details were collected yet - you can add them whenever you're ready, there's no deadline.
provide.whatChanges: The handler assigned to your case will be able to see the details you give below. They are encrypted when stored, the handler has to give a written reason to decrypt them, and every time anyone looks it is recorded.
provide.doneTitle: Your details are on the case
provide.doneBody: The handler assigned to your case can now find out who you are. Nobody else can, and nobody was told to ask you for this.
provide.alreadyChosenNote: This is the choice you already made when you filed your report - this is just where you follow through on it, whenever you want. Leaving this closed for now keeps your case exactly as it is.

followUpPrompt.submitAndOpenCase: Submit and open a new case

caseNotificationOptIn.noDetailsNote: A notification never contains any detail about your case — no message text, no category, nothing that could identify the report. It only tells you there is an update to come back and read here.
caseNotificationOptIn.getNotified: Get notified when there's a reply
caseNotificationOptIn.iosInstall: On iPhone and iPad, notifications only work once this site is added to your Home Screen. Tap the Share button in Safari, choose Add to Home Screen, then open Rectifia from your home screen and come back to this page to turn them on.

unsupported.title: Notifications aren't available in this browser
unsupported.body: This browser can't send you case updates. You can still come back any time with your Case ID and passcode to read replies.

blocked.title: Notifications are blocked for this site
blocked.body: Your browser is set to block notifications here, so we can't turn them on from this page. To allow them, open this site's permissions — usually the icon at the left of the address bar, or Settings → Site settings → Notifications — set notifications to Allow, then reload this page.

subscribed.title: You'll be notified of replies
subscribed.body: This device will get a notification when there's a reply on your case. It won't say anything about the case itself — just that there's an update to check.
subscribed.turnedOff: Notifications are off for this device. Reopen this page any time to turn them back on.
subscribed.sharedDeviceNote: On a shared or work device, turn notifications off before you leave — otherwise the next person using this browser will see the update prompts.

caseNotificationOptIn.turnOnBody: Turn on notifications on this device so you know when your handler responds, without having to keep checking back.

caseCredentialsHandoff.someFilesFailed_other: {{count}} files could not be attached. Your report was filed successfully regardless - once you have your Case ID and passcode, you can attach these files from your case thread instead.
caseCredentialsHandoff.keepPrivateOneLine: Keep these somewhere private. They cannot be reissued - without them there is no way back into the case.

caseFiled.title: Case filed
caseFiled.body: The report is now in the system and has been routed like any other case. The reporter has the same access to it as if they had filed it themselves — but only if you pass on the details below.

backdateWarning.title: This report was received some time ago
backdateWarning.body: Its compliance deadlines were calculated from the date you entered, not from today, so one or both may already have passed. That is the correct reading of the case — check the handler dashboard for what is now outstanding.

shownOnce.title: Shown once — these cannot be recovered
shownOnce.body1: The passcode is stored only as a hash. Nobody can look it up, reset it, or send it on: not you, not a Company Admin, not Rectifia.
shownOnce.strong: If you leave this screen without giving the reporter these details, they permanently lose access to their own case
shownOnce.body2: — they will not be able to read replies, answer the investigator's questions, or add anything they remember later.

caseCredentialsHandoff.linkFillsIn: The link fills in the Case ID. It does not contain the passcode, so on its own it opens nothing.
caseCredentialsHandoff.copyFailedNote: Couldn't copy automatically — select the details above and copy them.
caseCredentialsHandoff.downloadTradeoff: Saves a plain-text file to this device's usual downloads location. On a company-managed device, that file can be visible to IT, endpoint monitoring, or backup tools — including your employer's, if that's who this report is about.

beforeYouClose.title: Before you close this
beforeYouClose.handOver: Hand the Case ID and passcode to the reporter now, by whatever route they asked you to use.
beforeYouClose.dontKeepCopy: Don't keep a copy in your own notes, inbox, or a shared drive — a passcode sitting in a mailbox is a way into someone's case that outlives this conversation. If you use the download option above to hand these off, delete that file the same way once the reporter has the details, not just from your notes.
beforeYouClose.identityEncrypted: Their identity is encrypted and stored. It is not visible on any dashboard or in any case report, and reading it requires a Super Admin and a documented reason.
beforeYouClose.canReplyAnytime: The reporter can reply to the investigator and add information at any time using these details.

caseCredentialsHandoff.acknowledgment: I have given the Case ID and passcode to the reporter.

Their text is extracted and used as reference context when the system reasons about a case, so the questions asked and the evidence sought reflect the procedure your own rules require. Policy never decides an outcome, and reporters never see it.

adminBenchmarkPage.intro: The cross-company benchmark pool lets you see whether the shape of your closed cases is typical for your industry and headcount band, or an outlier. It is aggregate statistics only — never raw case data, never your company's identity, and cells below the anonymity thresholds are not published at all.

participation.title: Your participation
participation.description: Reading the pool requires contributing to it. A pool that can be read without contributing collapses into a one-way intelligence product, so both directions of participation are tied together.

withdrawCard.title: Withdraw
withdrawCard.description: Withdrawing takes effect at the next monthly recompute. Your contribution is removed completely — the pool is computed from scratch, not accumulated, so withdrawal is honest.
withdrawCard.body: After withdrawal your dashboard will no longer show benchmark comparisons, because reading requires contributing. You can opt back in at any time.

withdrawModal.body: Your data is removed from all published figures at the next monthly recomputation. After withdrawal your dashboard will no longer show benchmark comparisons, because reading requires contributing.

leaves.title: What leaves this company's boundary

withdraw.title: Withdrawing
withdraw.body: Withdrawing removes your company's contribution from the pool completely at the next monthly recomputation — the pool is recomputed from scratch each time, not accumulated, so nothing from your company lingers in a published figure after you leave.

coreQuestions.title: Standard questions
coreQuestions.description: Every company asks these four, in this order, unchanged. They cannot be edited, reordered, or removed.
coreQuestions.whyFixedBody: The wellbeing trend on an individual response, and the department averages your managers see, are calculated from these four answers and nothing else. Comparing this month against last month only means something if the question was identical both times. If the wording could change, a “declining” trend might just be a reworded question, and a department average might be averaging answers to two different questions — with no way to tell afterwards which had happened. Questions you add below appear in the survey and in what your HR Coordinator reads, but they never feed those numbers, which is exactly what makes them safe to change whenever you like.

pulseQuestionsPage.intro: What everyone on your roster is asked at each check-in. Four standard questions are fixed for every company; you can add up to {{max}} of your own.

neverPublished.title: Nothing published yet
neverPublished.body: Check-ins are not sent until a questionnaire is published, so nobody is being asked anything right now. Press Publish below to send the standard questions — with or without any of your own.

addedQuestions.title: Your added questions
addedQuestions.description: Optional, and yours to change. These appear in the survey and in what your HR Coordinator reads, but never affect the wellbeing trend or any department average.

pulseQuestionsPage.savedNotPublished: Saved, but not yet sent to anyone. Publish to make it live.

doNotAskWarning.title: Do not ask people to name other individuals
doNotAskWarning.body: A question that asks who someone's problem is with turns a wellness check into an informal reporting channel — without any of the protections the case system provides: no anonymity, no confidential handling, no investigation process, no retaliation follow-up. Answers here are shown to your HR Coordinator attributed to the employee who wrote them, by name. Keep these questions about how work feels, and let the reporting system handle reports.

pulseQuestionsPage.noAddedQuestions: No added questions. The four standard questions are asked on their own.
pulseQuestionsPage.questionPlaceholder: e.g. How clear were your priorities this week?
pulseQuestionsPage.everyQuestionNeedsText: Every added question needs some text.
pulseQuestionsPage.removalNotice: Removing a question stops it being asked from the next publish onwards. Answers already given to it are kept, and your HR Coordinator can still read them with the question they were answering — old responses are never rewritten.

preview.title: Preview
preview.description: The check-in exactly as employees receive it. This shows what is published and live, not your draft.

pulseQuestionsPage.sendTestHint: Sends a real check-in link to your own staff email address, and nowhere else. The response it records is marked as a test and never reaches an average or a trend.
pulseQuestionsPage.draftSaved: Draft saved. Nothing has changed for employees yet — press Publish to send it.
pulseQuestionsPage.publishedNotice: Published version {{version}}. Check-ins sent from now on use it; links already in someone's inbox keep the questions they were sent with.
pulseQuestionsPage.testSentNotice: A test check-in is on its way to {{email}}. It behaves exactly like a real one, and the response it records is excluded from every average and every trend.

publishModal.title: Publish this questionnaire?
publishModal.intro: Publishing does four things, and they are worth reading before you press it:
publishModal.bullet1: It becomes what everyone on your roster is asked at every check-in from now on.
publishModal.bullet2: It is saved as a permanent version. Old responses keep pointing at the version they answered, so nothing already collected changes meaning.
publishModal.bullet3: Check-in links already sitting in someone's inbox keep the questions they were sent with — they are not switched over mid-flight.
publishModal.bullet4: Your name and the time are recorded against it. This is a change to what your whole workforce is asked, so it has an author.

tierPreview.nothingToDelete: Nothing would be deleted on the next run.
tierPreview.recordsWouldBeDeleted_one: record would be deleted, spanning {{oldest}} to {{newest}}
tierPreview.recordsWouldBeDeleted_other: records would be deleted, spanning {{oldest}} to {{newest}}
tierPreview.truncatedNote: (count is a floor - more match than were scanned)

retentionPage.holdReleasedNotice: Legal hold released on case {{caseId}}. It is now eligible for the next retention sweep.
retentionPage.summary: Closed cases are permanently deleted {{caseDuration}} after closure. Reporter identities are deleted after {{identityDuration}}. This cannot be undone.
retentionPage.intro: How long this company keeps case data before it is permanently deleted, and which cases are currently frozen against deletion by a legal hold. Deletion here is hard deletion - there is no soft-delete flag, no archive, and no recovery window.

identityRetentionDays.label: Reporter identity & contact data
identityRetentionDays.description: reporterIdentity, contactEmail, and push subscriptions - purged on this clock once a case is closed. Once an investigation is closed there is almost never a lawful basis to keep knowing who filed it.

caseRetentionDays.label: Case content
caseRetentionDays.description: The case narrative, messages, questionnaire answers, and evidence files - hard-deleted this many days after the case CLOSES, never from when it was created.

pulseResponseRetentionDays.label: Pulse Check responses
pulseResponseRetentionDays.description: Individual Pulse Check answers. The aggregated, k-anonymised summaries survive this window - only the individual responses that fed them are deleted.

auditLogRetentionDays.label: Audit logs
auditLogRetentionDays.description: identityAccessAuditLog, triageAccessLog, staffIntakeAuditLog and evidenceAccessLog. These run on their own clock and outlive the case they describe - a log proving who decrypted an identity is worthless if it is destroyed on the same schedule as the thing it protects.

clampedWarning.title: A stored value now exceeds your jurisdiction's ceiling
clampedWarning.item: {{label}}: currently stored as {{stored}} days, but will be clamped to {{clampedTo}} days on the next retention run. This happens automatically - saving new values below will not retroactively change what happened to any data already purged.

shorteningWarning.title: This shortens at least one window
shorteningWarning.body: Run a preview below before saving - a shortened window deletes more, sooner, and this cannot be undone once the next sweep runs.

retentionPage.previewFirstHint: Preview this exact change before saving.

previewCard.title: Preview next sweep
previewCard.description: A dry run against the values above - shows what would be permanently deleted the next time the retention sweep runs. Deletes nothing.
previewCard.hint: Run a preview to see counts before saving.
previewCard.stale: These results are for a previously entered set of values, not the ones currently in the form. Run the preview again to see the current values.

legalHolds.title: Legal holds
legalHolds.description: A case on legal hold is skipped by every retention sweep, including the identity-purge tier - litigation freezes identity data too. Restricted to Company Admin and Super Admin.
legalHolds.reasonPlaceholder: Why this case must be frozen against deletion (min. 10 characters).
legalHolds.empty: No cases currently on legal hold

crisisContact.title: Crisis contact

crisisContact.namePlaceholder: e.g. Dr. Jordan Lee, EAP counsellor
crisisContact.hint: A name is required, plus at least one way to reach them — an email, a phone number, or both. This can be an external provider such as an Employee Assistance Programme; they do not need a login on this platform.

pulseCadence.awaitingContactHint: On the roster but with no email
pulseCadence.awaitingContactNotice_one: {{count}} roster member has no email on file, so their invite waits until an address is added. Add one on the <link>Employees</link> page.
pulseCadence.awaitingContactNotice_other: {{count}} roster members have no email on file, so their invite waits until an address is added. Add one on the <link>Employees</link> page.

pulseCadence.addEmployeesHint: Add employees before sending a check-in.

sendNowModal.title: Send a pulse check now?
sendNowModal.body_one: This queues a check-in for {{count}} active employee right away, regardless of the cadence schedule. Any outstanding pulse-check links are superseded — an employee still holding an older link will be sent a fresh one instead.
sendNowModal.body_other: This queues a check-in for {{count}} active employees right away, regardless of the cadence schedule. Any outstanding pulse-check links are superseded — an employee still holding an older link will be sent a fresh one instead.
sendNowModal.awaitingContactNotice_one: {{count}} of them has no email on file and will wait for an address before delivery.
sendNowModal.awaitingContactNotice_other: {{count}} of them have no email on file and will wait for an address before delivery.

jurisdictions.title: Jurisdictions
jurisdictions.description: The jurisdictions this company operates in. Compliance deadlines follow the strictest one selected.
jurisdictions.deprecated: {{label}} — deprecated, can be removed, cannot be re-added
jurisdictions.atLeastOneRequired: At least one jurisdiction is required.
jurisdictions.strictestNotice: Default compliance timeline follows {{jurisdiction}}, the strictest of the selected jurisdictions.
jurisdictions.changeNotice: Changing jurisdictions affects deadline computation for future cases only. Deadlines are set when a case is created and are not recomputed for cases that already exist.

timeZone.title: Time zone
timeZone.enterHint: Enter an IANA time zone identifier, e.g. "Europe/London".
timeZone.decidesHint: This decides the local hour deadline escalations and pulse-check invitations go out at, not when compliance deadlines themselves fall due.
timeZone.invalid: Not a recognised time zone. Use an IANA identifier such as "America/New_York".

followUp.title: Retaliation follow-up check-ins
followUp.description: After a case closes, reporters get neutral check-ins asking whether anything has changed. This applies to all categories by default — retaliation can follow any report.
followUp.daysLabel: Days after closure to check in
followUp.checkInsSummary_one: {{count}} check-in at day {{days}} after a case closes.
followUp.checkInsSummary_other: {{count}} check-ins at day {{days}} after a case closes.
followUp.categoriesHint: All on by default. Untick a category to stop scheduling check-ins for cases closed in it.
followUp.neutralNotice: Check-ins are neutral and optional for the reporter. A reporter can always answer that nothing has changed, or ignore them entirely — there is no chasing. Changes here apply to cases closed from now on.

noResponse.label: Unknown — no response
noResponse.hint: Reporter did not return. This is not evidence that nothing happened.

followUpStatus.title: Retaliation follow-ups
followUpStatus.description: Post-closure check-ins with reporters. Metadata only — the reporter's answer stays with the handler of any case they choose to file.

empty.title: No follow-ups yet
empty.description: Follow-ups are scheduled automatically when a case closes.

followUpStatus.concernNotice_one: {{count}} reporter indicated something happened after their case closed. If they chose to file, it is a new, separate case in the queue with its own handler.
followUpStatus.concernNotice_other: {{count}} reporters indicated something happened after their case closed. If they chose to file, it is a new, separate case in the queue with its own handler.
followUpStatus.noResponseFootnote: “Unknown — no response” means the reporter did not return, which is the expected case for an anonymous reporter. It is not a sign that nothing happened.

policyUpload.couldNotProcess: The document could not be processed.

processingFailed.body: The document was saved but has no usable text, so it will not ground any cases. You can delete it and try a different file.

patternService.describeSignal_one: {{count}} case in this department and role tier in the last {{windowDays}} days.
patternService.describeSignal_other: {{count}} cases in this department and role tier in the last {{windowDays}} days.
patternService.describeSignal_crossCategory_one: {{count}} case across different categories in this department and role tier in the last {{windowDays}} days.
patternService.describeSignal_crossCategory_other: {{count}} cases across different categories in this department and role tier in the last {{windowDays}} days.
patternService.caseCountCaveat: This counts cases, not people. Reports are anonymous, so one person filing several times and several people filing once look identical here.
patternService.crossCategoryCaveat: These cases are of different kinds. That is weaker than a cluster of the same kind of report and should not be read as repeated conduct.

patternSignals.title: Pattern signals
patternSignals.description: Repeat reports grouped by department and role tier over the last {{windowDays}} days. Recomputed daily.

empty.title: No pattern signals
empty.description: No department and role tier reached the reporting threshold in the last {{windowDays}} days.

suppressionNotice.title: Not enough people in this group to report safely
suppressionNotice.body_one: {{count}} group reached the threshold but was withheld: fewer than {{minPopulation}} employees match the department and role tier. In a group that small, a department and a role tier identify a person, so the signal is not shown at all rather than shown less precisely.
suppressionNotice.body_other: {{count}} groups reached the threshold but were withheld: fewer than {{minPopulation}} employees match the department and role tier. In a group that small, a department and a role tier identify a person, so the signal is not shown at all rather than shown less precisely.
suppressionNotice.body_missingDirectory_one: {{count}} group reached the threshold but was withheld: fewer than {{minPopulation}} employees match the department and role tier, or the employee directory has no entry for that department. In a group that small, a department and a role tier identify a person, so the signal is not shown at all rather than shown less precisely.
suppressionNotice.body_missingDirectory_other: {{count}} groups reached the threshold but were withheld: fewer than {{minPopulation}} employees match the department and role tier, or the employee directory has no entry for that department. In a group that small, a department and a role tier identify a person, so the signal is not shown at all rather than shown less precisely.
suppressionNotice.footnote_one: Which group deliberately is not named here - naming it would be the same disclosure.
suppressionNotice.footnote_other: Which groups deliberately are not named here - naming them would be the same disclosure.

relatedPatternNotice.title: Part of a pattern signal - {{signalType}}
relatedPatternNotice.dateRange: First {{first}}, most recent {{last}}. This case is one of them.
relatedPatternNotice.informationalOnly: Informational only. It does not suggest a finding or an action on this case, and the other cases behind this count are not yours to read.

consistencyInsights.noRankedActions: No ranked actions recorded for this segment yet.
consistencyInsights.insufficientDataBody_one: {{count}} closed case on file for this category — not enough for the Consistency Engine to establish a reliable pattern yet. This is expected for a new or low-volume category, not an error.
consistencyInsights.insufficientDataBody_other: {{count}} closed cases on file for this category — not enough for the Consistency Engine to establish a reliable pattern yet. This is expected for a new or low-volume category, not an error.
consistencyInsights.noDepartmentTier: No department tier within this category reached the reporting threshold on its own, even though the category total did.

consistencyInsights.description: Where this company's own historical outcomes sit, per category and seniority tier. Aggregate only — no single case's score or action is shown.

empty.title: No consistency data yet

benchmarkComparison.insufficientDataBody: This cell has not reached the minimum of 5 contributing companies and 25 cases required before any figure is published. This is common and normal, not an error — the pool grows as more companies opt in.
benchmarkComparison.title: Industry benchmark
benchmarkComparison.description: How this company's closed cases compare to the wider pool for your industry and size band. Aggregate statistics only — no other company is named, no case is exposed, and cells below the anonymity thresholds are not published at all.

notOptedIn.title: Not opted in
notOptedIn.body: The cross-company benchmark pool is opt-in. Your Company Admin can enable it on the company Benchmark page. Reading the pool requires contributing to it — a pool that can be read without contributing collapses into a one-way intelligence product.

incomplete.title: Cell coordinates missing
incomplete.body: Your opt-in record's industry or employee count no longer places this company inside a valid cell. Ask your Company Admin to re-opt-in with the current headcount.

noCells.title: No cells for your segment yet
noCells.description: No category cell has reached the reporting thresholds for your industry and size band. This is common and normal — the pool grows as more companies opt in.

benchmarkComparison.roundingFootnote: Cells publish only when at least 5 companies and 25 cases contribute; below either threshold nothing is published at all, so an "insufficient data" row is not an error. Every published figure is rounded — medians, percentages to the nearest 5 — because unrounded values over small populations leak more than they inform.
